results.content: # CI/CD pipeline for my PHP web application. How can I set up a CI/CD pipeline for my PHP web application, which is hosted in Azure Repos? I am utilizing Azure DevOps to set up the CI/CD pipeline. * In Azure DevOps → Project Settings → Service Connections → New → SSH. trigger: branches: include: - main pool: vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest' steps: # Install PHP dependencies - script: | composer install displayName: 'Install dependencies' # Package the app - task: ArchiveFiles@2 inputs: rootFolderOrFile: '$(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)' includeRootFolder: false archiveType: 'zip' archiveFile: '$(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)/app.zip' replaceExistingArchive: true - task: PublishBuildArtifacts@1 inputs: PathtoPublish: '$(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)/app.zip' ArtifactName: 'drop'. from there you can outsource your CI/CD pipeline to GitHub which can also automatically deploy your code to azure. results.title: CI/CD inputs | GitLab Docs
results.content: To define specific values when the pipeline runs, use inputs instead of CI/CD variables. * **Modification**: Once passed at pipeline initialization, input values are interpolated in the CI/CD configuration and remain fixed for the entire pipeline run. Use `spec:inputs` in the CI/CD configuration header to define input parameters that can be passed to the configuration file. * Inputs can use CI/CD variables, but have the same variable limitations as the `include` keyword. You should always set default values when using inputs to configure new pipelines with any method other than `include`. * `spec:inputs:default` to define default values for inputs when not specified. When an input replaces an entire YAML value in the CI/CD configuration, it is interpolated into the configuration as its specified type. Use `include:inputs` to set the values for inputs when the included configuration is added to the pipeline, including for:. For example, to include and set the input values for `scan-website-job.yml` from the input configuration example:. Inputs for pipelines must be defined in the `spec:inputs` header of the main `.gitlab-ci.yml` file. You cannot use inputs defined in included files for pipeline-level configuration. You should always set default values when defining inputs for pipelines. You can pass inputs to downstream pipelines, if the downstream pipeline’s configuration file uses `spec:inputs`. You can reuse input definitions across multiple CI/CD configurations by defining them in external files and including them with `spec:include`. Then you can include the external inputs in your `.gitlab-ci.yml` with `local`:. If you define an input in both an included input file, and the `inputs:` section in the `.gitlab-ci.yml` configuration, the inputs from the file are overridden. In this example, assuming the input uses the default value and `$MY_VAR` is an unmasked project variable with value `my value`:. Use `expand_vars` to expand CI/CD variables in the input value. Use `posix_escape` to escape any POSIX *Bourne shell* control or meta characters that might be included in input values.

results.content: To set up a pipeline, you need to define a `.gitlab-ci.yml` file in the root directory of your repository. gitlab-ci.yml example for python Here’s an example `.gitlab-ci.yml` file that runs a Python script: In this example, a single job named `test_job` is defined under the `test` stage. 1. **Commit and push the `.gitlab-ci.yml` file:** Once you have defined the CI/CD pipeline configuration, commit and push the `.gitlab-ci.yml` file to the GitLab repository. 2. **Trigger the pipeline:** After pushing the changes, GitLab will automatically detect the `.gitlab-ci.yml` file and start running the pipeline defined in it. Your Python script will be executed whenever the CI/CD pipeline is triggered in GitLab. You can further customize the pipeline to include additional stages, jobs, and commands as per your requirements. How do I create a CI CD pipeline for Python project? To create a CI/CD pipeline for a Python project, you can use GitLab’s built-in CI/CD feature. 3. **Define stages and jobs:** In the `.gitlab-ci.yml` file, define the stages and jobs for your pipeline. Here’s an example of running tests using `pytest`: - pip install -r requirements.txt Make sure to include the necessary commands specific to your project, such as setting up a virtual environment or executing specific Python scripts. 2. **Monitor pipeline execution:** GitLab will automatically detect the `.gitlab-ci.yml` file and start running the pipeline whenever changes are pushed to the repository. Your CI/CD pipeline is now set up for your Python project. Yes, GitLab supports Python as one of the programming languages for CI/CD pipelines. GitLab provides a built-in CI/CD feature that allows you to automate the testing, building, and deployment of your Python projects. With GitLab CI/CD, you can define a `.gitlab-ci.yml` file in your repository to configure the pipeline. In the jobs defined in the `.gitlab-ci.yml` file, you can use Python commands and scripts to perform various tasks, such as installing dependencies, running tests, building your project, and deploying it to a server or a cloud platform. You can use these tools within your pipeline to ensure a smooth CI/CD workflow for your Python projects. Overall, GitLab is a capable and widely used platform for implementing CI/CD pipelines for Python projects.

results.title: Run Playwright Tests via GitLab CI/CD Pipeline | Medium
results.content: # Run Playwright Tests via GitLab CI/CD Pipeline using project-level variables, saving results to artifacts. In this project we will create and clone a GitLab repository, install Playwright and generating basic tests and run Playwright tests via GitLab CI/CD pipeline. We will use GitLab project-level variables and publish Playwright test results as pipeline artefacts viewable via GitLab pages. Next we’re going to configure the pipeline to run the tests and publish the results and create a global variable for BASE\_URL in GitLab project settings. # Variablesvariables: BASE_URL: $BASE_URL # variable defined in GitLab Project CI/CD Settings# Define the stages for your pipelinestages: - test# Define the job for running Playwright testsrun_playwright_tests: stage: test image: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.39.0-jammy script: - npm ci # Install project dependencies - npx playwright test # Run your Playwright tests  - echo "https://$CI_PROJECT_NAMESPACE.gitlab.io/-/$CI_PROJECT_NAME/-/jobs/$CI_JOB_ID/artifacts/playwright-report/index.html" # print the URL to view the results allow_failure: true # Publish Playwright test results as artifacts and keep for 2 daysartifacts: when: always paths: - playwright-report expire_in: 2 days.
